issue_context.title: AsnWriter.WriteObjectIdentifier permits invalid sub identifier
issue_context.body:
### Description

"ITU-T X.680 | ISO/IEC 8824-1 requires that there be only three arcs allocated from the root node (with primary integer values of 0, 1, and 2), and at most forty arcs from the first two of these arcs (with primary integer values of 0 to 39)."

However, `WriteObjectIdentifier` does not validate this. This results in non-roundtrippable encoding.

Given that `WriteObjectIdentifier` goes through the trouble of doing other validations on the input, this seems like an oversight in validating when the root arc is 0 or 1.

### Reproduction Steps

Consider

```C#
AsnWriter asnWriter = new(AsnEncodingRules.DER);
asnWriter.WriteObjectIdentifier("1.255.3.0.9");
AsnReader reader = new (asnWriter.Encode(), AsnEncodingRules.DER);
Console.WriteLine(reader.ReadObjectIdentifier());
```

This will print out "2.215.3.0.9".

### Expected behavior

Throw "System.ArgumentException: The OID value is invalid. (Parameter 'oidValue')" like when the root arc is invalid.

### Actual behavior

Encodes incorrectly with no error.

### Regression?

Not a regression.

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

Impacts all versions of System.Formats.Asn1.

### Other information

_No response_
